Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. Since those subs went the other way, this growth is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

insights.title: Installs to subs, by app — YCV is turning installs into New Subs worse than usual (-3.6% vs Install +4.2%).
insights.body: Some apps are not converting installs into subscribers at their usual rate: YCV New Subs -3.6% vs Install +4.2% (worse than its installs); YMK New Subs -6.8% vs Install +4.4% (worse than its installs). Revenue follows about a week later, so these are the apps to watch next week.

insights.title: Which app — App Total Revenue -4.4% is mostly YCP — not every app.
insights.body: App Total Revenue moved -4.4% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -4.4%, YMK -1.8%, YCP -7.5%, YCV -1.6%). YCP accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Which country — MX is out of line with every other country on App Total Revenue (+55.1% vs -1.8%).
insights.body: For YMK, App Total Revenue in MX is +55.1% while all countries together are -1.8% — a gap of +56.9pp. MX is about 2% of revenue, so it is big enough to be worth a look.

insights.title: Market trend — BR is losing ground fast on turning installs into subs (-16.9%, now 11.1%).
insights.body: In BR, 11.1% of installs now turn into new subs — -16.9% versus last period. It is about 5% of revenue (a market worth watching): fewer of the people downloading are subscribing, and revenue will feel that within a week or two.

insights.title: Best and worst markets — GB turns installs into new subs best of anywhere (20.6% vs 13.1% overall).
insights.body: In GB, 20.6% of installs turn into new subs, versus 13.1% across all markets and apps (+7.6pp difference). That is much better than the rest — worth understanding and copying. GB is about 5% of revenue. Its App Total New Subs is -22.3% this period.

insights.title: Install source — App Total Install +3.3% came from all three channels, not from one.
insights.body: App Total Install was 33,389, against 32,334 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of +1,055. Where that came from: Organic Install +429 (41% of the change, +2.8%), Paid Install +427 (41% of the change, +3.1%), SEO Install +196 (19% of the change, +8.3%). No single channel accounts for as much as 45% of the change, so this is not about one channel's ad spend or search ranking — look for something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Next period outlook — No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
insights.body: App Total New Subs is -6.4% and App Total Install is +3.3%; the gap between them (-9.6pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal.
